name: Ambros
status: Ambros founded the shared predecessor empire of Veldrassen and Ostrevain. His killing of a Hunter with a sword is the undisputed core of his legend; the encounter’s circumstances remain unknown.
empire: Ambros founded the empire from which Veldrassen and Ostrevain eventually emerged. A warrior, teacher, sorcerer and lawgiver, he united a substantial part of the inhabited world, without establishing permanent planetary unity. Founded well before the last major culling, his empire fragmented across subsequent generations under succession disputes, human warfare and repeated cullings. Its exact boundaries and dates remain incompletely reconstructed. Veldrassen emphasises the unifier who bound different peoples together; Ostrevain emphasises the sovereign whose authority held them together. Both claim his inheritance through differing political traditions; neither claim establishes a surviving bloodline.
duel: Above all, Ambros is remembered as the man who killed a Hunter with a sword. That act is the undisputed core of his legend, inseparable from his identity and more famous than the empire he founded. The uncertainty concerns the circumstances, not whether his sword killed the Hunter. No reliable account establishes whether it was fully armed and armoured, had missing or damaged equipment, was hunting Ambros, was ambushed, or had already been wounded in a crash or another encounter. The precise role of his psychic abilities is likewise unknown. None of these possibilities is an established explanation, and the tradition does not prove a formal duel against a fresh, fully equipped opponent.
gift: He is remembered as an exceptionally rare psychic talent as well as a warrior and lawgiver. Later tellings mingle historical deeds with prophecy, miracles and moral teaching. The intended historical figure is a remarkable human psyker, not proof of literal divinity or of a hidden identity from established offworld lore.
legacy: Before Ambros, the remembered human victories over Hunters were extraordinarily rare: craft brought down by artillery, occasional ambushes, or concentrated firearms overwhelming an individual. Killing one in melee was unheard of. Hunters were stronger, faster and more tactically capable than ordinary humans; even military personnel with firearms and artillery rarely killed them. The sword killing therefore travelled farther than imperial proclamations. It showed that Hunters were flesh and blood, not unkillable wraiths: ordinary physical means could kill them, and one person could make a difference. People embraced and spread the legend because it gave them hope, without making the feat easy or commonplace. Songs, oral histories, surviving texts and concealed archives carry both the deed and fragments of Ambros’s teachings and imperial law across the culling eras. Local beliefs and interpretations differ; his legacy does not require a single planetary religion.
continuity: This establishes background for future play, not a recovered artefact, a new ability, a solved historical mystery or knowledge automatically acquired by Galahad. No specific surviving relic, bloodline, capital or date is assigned.
